Avery Johnson: Anyone have an EMEA-friendly demo variant / slide bullets that emphasize data residency + private/VPC? Getting this a lot w/ UK + DACH prospects. Want something crisp I can drop into the talk track.

Lukas Meyer: Yep — for EMEA I usually re-order the story a bit. Top bullets that land:
- “Choose your processing region” (EU regions available) + policy-based routing by region.
- “No cross-region failover unless you explicitly enable it.” (Say this early, they always ask.)
- Private deployment option: VPC / on-prem for strict residency + regulated workloads.
- Audit logs + retention controls (who did what, when; configurable retention) — helps security + procurement.

Lukas Meyer: Also, procurement pacing here is slower, so I frame it as: start hosted in EU region for speed → move to Dedicated EU capacity for predictability → Private for strict controls. Same API/SDK the whole way.

Hannah Schmitt: +1. Specific phrasing that’s been safe:
- “You can pin a region for inference and keep traffic in-region.”
- “Fallback is configurable: same-region first; cross-region is opt-in.”
- “We support Private deployments where the control plane is isolated and networking is customer-managed.”

Hannah Schmitt: What NOT to say (learned the hard way): blanket “data never leaves the EU” without the qualifier that *you* choose region + retention settings. Better: “We give you controls to keep data in-region and minimize data stored.”

Avery Johnson: Amazing. Do you have the 3-4 slide version? Or a snippet I can paste into speaker notes?

Lukas Meyer: I don’t think we have a finalized mini-deck yet. But here’s the talk-track chunk I use (feel free to copy):

Lukas Meyer: 
"For EMEA teams, the first question is usually data residency. In Redwood you can explicitly choose the processing region and route traffic by policy so requests stay in-region. Reliability still matters, so we support fallback — but by default we keep fallback within the same region, and cross-region is something you opt into. If you need tighter guarantees, we can go from Hosted in an EU region to Dedicated EU capacity, and for strict environments we support Private deployments in your VPC or on-prem — same interface, same observability, same rollout controls." 

Soojin Lee: This is super helpful. I can add an EMEA “module” slide in the appendix with these bullets + approved language. Markus/Simran — do we have a clean architecture screenshot for “Hosted EU + Dedicated EU + Private VPC” we can use as backup mode?

Markus Klein: We have a draft diagram from the Private deck (not polished). I can grab screenshots from Console showing region pin + routing policy for backup. Will DM you links.

Simran Kaur: For security reviewers, the clarifier slide I like is:
- Data path: request payload → inference runtime in selected region/VPC
- Control plane separation (what metadata is stored where)
- Logging/retention knobs (how to turn down storage)
If we keep it to that, we avoid over-promising.

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: Also, do we have a one-liner on sub-processors / DPA? It comes up right after residency.

Hannah Schmitt: I usually punt that to “we’ll share DPA + sub-processor list in security review,” but you can say: “We have standard DPAs available and can support enterprise security reviews.” Don’t go deep live unless they ask.

Lukas Meyer: Agree. In the demo, keep it to: region controls + Private option + audit logs. Then offer follow-up package (SOC2, DPA, subprocessors) as next step. Otherwise it derails.

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- I’ll draft an “EMEA / Data Residency” appendix slide w/ approved bullets + talk track snippet.
- Markus to provide 2–3 backup screenshots (routing policy + region selection + audit log view) for when the live environment is flaky.
I’ll post the draft in #sales once ready.

Markus Klein: :eyes: Will do. Also note: in the demo tenant we should avoid showing any region toggle that implies global by default. I’ll double-check our seeded routes are pinned EU for the EMEA variant.

Avery Johnson: Perfect. Thanks all — this will save me a bunch of back-and-forth on calls.
